2. Dust a work surface and the dough ball with a little flour to prevent sticking. Flatten dough with a rolling pin until it forms a thin disk large enough to be draped over the pie plate or bowl.
3. Freeze the dough for 20 minutes, or for the duration of filling prep and cooking.
4. Combine the oil, wine, and soy sauce to make a marinade. Submerge the beef in the marinade, and let this marinate in the fridge for 24 hours.
5. Remove the meat from the marinade, and slice it ¼ inch thick.
6. Heat the saucepan over high heat, then add the butter and let it melt.
7. Add the sliced beef to the saucepan. Sauté, stirring, until browned all over.
8. Add bay leaf, thyme, basil, celery, onion, and carrot. Sauté, stirring occasionally, until onions and celery are soft.
9. Scrape some of the fond off the pan bottom without taking it out, if possible. Stir in the wine, Worcestershire sauce, and gravy granules for 1 minute
10. Turn heat to low, stir in ketchup, and cover the pan. Cook until stew volume is reduced by a third to half and liquids are beginning to thicken.
11. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
12. Remove from the heat, and discard the bay leaf.
13. Pour filling into the pie plate or bowl.
14. Cover with the pie crust disk and press around edges to seal. The dough falling apart is acceptable as long as it retains an amount of crunch or flakiness.
15. Bake at 445 °F (230 °C / Gas 8) for 10 to 15 minutes or until top crust turns medium brown. Handle with care.
ingredient_lines: 3 tbsp butter or margarine, cut into small cubes
¼ cup red wine or lemon juice
½ stalk celery, sliced ⅛ inch thick
⅓ whole carrot, sliced ⅛ inch thick, then cut into semicircles
notes: The butter/margarine can be substituted by 2 tbsp olive oil mixed with 1 tbsp milk.
The gravy granules can be substituted by 1 tsp beef bouillon mixed with 2 tsp hot water.

If you want a bottom crust for the pie, double the dough quantities, and divide the dough in half before rolling out each portion. Grease the baking dish and line it with one of the dough disks before freezing and filling.
You can also slice the steak before marinating it in order to facilitate the flavor permeation. You may not need to marinate for as long if you do so.
image_files: Steak and Wine Pie by Jarrod Baniqued.jpg

title: Spinach Mushroom Omelet
instructions:
1. In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, salt, pepper, nutmeg and milk, until even and glossy.
2. Heat the skillet over medium heat. Add half the butter, tilting the skillet in a circular motion to coat evenly.
3. Add paprika, mushrooms, and onions, and sauté until lightly browned.
4. Add spinach and toss for 30 seconds, or until slightly wilted, but still crunchy. Remove the vegetables from the heat and set aside.
5. Add the remaining half of the oil or butter to the pan over medium heat, and coat evenly. Lower the heat.
6. Pour the egg mixture into the skillet, swirling the pan to ensure an even, creamy layer of eggs. Heat until the eggs have begun to set, with some fluff on top.
7. Top the egg layer with the vegetables, distributing the vegetables evenly. Sprinkle the cheese evenly on top.
8. Gently push the edges of the omelet half a centimeter toward the center of the skillet with two spatulas, making sure not to break it. Turn the heat off.
9. Use the spatulas to carefully lift/pull half the omelet off the skillet and fold it over the other half. Carefully move the entire omelet onto a plate and serve.
ingredient_lines: ⅔ cup baby bella mushrooms, thinly sliced
½ ea. large red onion, diced
½ cup shredded aged cheddar cheese
notes: If you want to prevent the mushrooms from browning after you slice them, submerge them in a bowl of cool water until ready to cook them. Drain before adding to the pan.

title: Fribourg Omelet
instructions:
1. In a large bowl, whisk together the eggs, salt, pepper, milk and nutmeg, until even and glossy.
2. Place half the butter in the skillet on medium heat. Swirl the pan to coat evenly with butter.
3. Add ham and cook until deep brown.
4. Stir in kale for 30 seconds, or until slightly wilted but still crunchy. Set aside the ham and greens.
5. Add the remainder of the butter to the skillet over low heat.
6. Pour egg mixture into the skillet, moving skillet to create a flat, even layer. Heat until the eggs have begun to set, with some fluff on top.
7. Scatter the ham and kale evenly over the top of the eggs.
8. Lay the Gruyère slices over the open omelet. Heat until the edges of the cheese have melted slightly.
9. Gently push the edges of the omelet less than half a centimeter toward the center of the skillet with two spatulas, making sure not to break it. Turn the heat off.
10. Use the spatulas to lift half the omelet and fold over the other half. Move the entire omelet carefully onto a plate and serve.
ingredient_lines: 3 thin slices of ham, cut in small squares

title: Veggie Pizza
instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 240° C (450° F / Gas 9).
2. Brush the dough surface with olive oil.
3. Ladle the sauce over the dough, spreading it evenly.
4. Distribute the cheeses evenly over the crust.
5. Lay the toppings evenly over the cheese. If needed, press toppings down with a utensil to provide clearance from the oven ceiling. If desired, top the vegetables with extra cheese and sauce to hold vegetables down.
6. Bake pizza in oven until crust edges are deep dark brown (roughly 15 minutes for pre-made crust, much longer for freshly made dough).
7. Take pizza out of oven and let cool.
ingredient_lines: 1 pre-made pizza crust, rolled to 30 cm (12 inches) across
½ ea. green bell pepper, de-seeded and thinly sliced
½ cup thinly sliced baby bella mushrooms
4½ tbsp pitted and sliced black olives

attribution: Wikibooks — Cookbook:Kuku Sabzi with Potato Slices
title: Kuku Sabzi with Potato Slices
instructions:
1. In a large bowl, whisk the eggs, salt, pepper, nutmeg and milk, until glossy and even.
2. Rinse the potato slices and transfer to a bowl. Cover with hot water and soak for 10 minutes to remove excess starch. Drain away the excess water.
3. Fry the potato slices in a skillet with the paprika and half of the butter until the potatoes are soft, tender and brown. Tilt the pan in a circular motion to coat potatoes evenly.
4. Add the onions and herbs and stir thoroughly, then sauté until onions are soft and translucent.
5. Add the remaining half of the butter to the skillet. Stir contents thoroughly to evenly coat with the fat, then lower the heat.
6. Pour the beaten eggs into the skillet, tilting the skillet in a circular motion until vegetables are bound with the eggs. Heat until the eggs have set on the sides.
7. Using the spatulas and taking care not to break it, fold the edges of the kuku sabzi a centimeter toward the center, forming a large disk with a brown crust on the bottom. Turn the heat off and let skillet cool slightly.
8. Place a plate on the skillet and carefully flip the skillet over to unmold the disk of eggs.
9. Return the egg disk to the skillet, with the uncooked side on the bottom and the crust on top. Turn the heat to high, cook until the crust forms on the bottom, and remove from the heat.
10. Using the spatula, pull and lift the browned kuku sabzi off the skillet, onto plate, and serve.
ingredient_lines: ½ bunch fresh cilantro, finely chopped
½ bunch fresh dill, finely chopped
1 tbsp finely chopped dried fenugreek leaves

title: Breakfast Dürüm
instructions:
1. Brush the flatbread with the tablespoon of water to keep it soft. Toast the bread using a skillet or in a toaster oven until brown on edges. Set aside.
2. Combine the grated potato with half the hot water in a bowl. Let sit for 3 minutes, then stir thoroughly and drain the water from the bowl. Repeat this process with the remaining hot water, then drain the potatoes in a colander. Shake gently in a horizontal motion to remove excess starch and water, then set aside to dry.
3. Sauté the mushrooms in 1 tbsp butter. Add spinach, and cook on medium heat until slightly wilted.
4. Whisk together the eggs, seasonings and milk, then pour over the spinach and mushrooms. When the eggs are half-set, sprinkle the cheddar on top, then fold the omelet in half and remove from the skillet.
5. Heat the remaining butter in the skillet. Turn the heat to high, then add the potatoes, onions, and steak, evenly and fully covering the bottom of the skillet. Season to taste, then let them sear to your desired brownness and crunch, taking care to turn them over. Remove from the heat.
6. Assemble the dürüm by laying the bread sheet flat, with the longer edges to the left and right sides. Spreading the hummus evenly on the half of the bread farthest from you. Pile the potato mixture and the omelet evenly on the nearest half. Pinch and fold the nearest edge over, then roll into a 5-cm (2-inch) thick cylinder and serve.
ingredient_lines: 1 large sheet of lavash or yufka flatbread
4 tbsp butter or olive oil, divided
½ cup thinly sliced baby bella or Crimini mushrooms
5 thin slices cooked beef sirloin or flank

title: Supercharger Tea
instructions:
1. Place tea bags in French press or coffee pot. Make sure to keep the strings taut to prevent the paper weights from falling in.
2. Pour the hot water into French press. Place lid on top, with a tight grip on the paper weights.
3. Let the tea steep for 5 minutes.
4. If using a French press, slowly push the plunger onto the bags, again with a tight grip on the paper weights.
5. Take off the lid, scoop the teabags out, and gently squeeze the brew from the bags before disposing of them.
6. Add sweetener and stir thoroughly.
7. Let tea cool to room temperature. Serve over ice, or place open pot in freezer for 70 minutes for quicker cooling. Stir in milk or citrus juice before serving.

title: Grenadine Soda
instructions: 1. Combine grenadine and carbonated water until well-mixed.
notes: Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original Sparkling Water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.

title: Date Soda
instructions:
1. Combine syrup and carbonated water until evenly mixed.
2. Serve cold.
notes: Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original Sparkling Water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.

title: Date Syrup
instructions:
1. Bring the water to a boil, and pour it over the dates in a heat-proof bowl.
2. Let the dates soak for around half an hour.
3. Use a blender to purée the date-water mixture.
4. Transfer the mixture to a pot, and simmer over medium heat for 1 hour.
5. Remove the mixture from the heat and allow to cool to room temperature.
6. Strain the mixture through several layers of cheesecloth or a nut milk bag.
7. Return the strained liquid to a pot, and simmer until it reaches your desired syrup consistency. Keep in mind that it will thicken after cooling—if you have a thermometer, you can use it to monitor the sugar concentration, aiming for somewhere between 104–113°C (219–235°F).
8. Remove from the heat and allow to cool.
ingredient_lines: 1 cup (120 ml) Medjool dates, seeds removed
notes: Be careful while mixing the syrup; hot sugar can splash and cause serious burns.
You can use this syrup to make date soda.

title: Vegan Gingerbread Cake
instructions:
1. Combine the flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg, salt, and sugar in the large bowl.
2. Whisk together the almond milk, coconut oil, applesauce, molasses, and vanilla in the medium bowl.
3. Mix the wet with the dry ingredients successively.
4. Grease the baking pan and fill it with the batter.
5. Bake for 12 minutes at 190 °C (375 °F) or until it tests clean when a skewer is inserted into the center.
6. Cool and unmold the cake.
ingredient_lines: 1 cup (240 ml) all-purpose flour or a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend
⅓ cup (240 ml) granulated cane sugar
2 tablespoon (15 ml) coconut oil, melted and cooled
notes: Choose a baking pan with dimensions that will ensure the cake is just a few centimeters high.

title: Lemon-Lime Soda II
instructions:
1. Combine the spirit or gum arabic water and oils together in a small cup, mixing well. Set aside.
2. Transfer this mixture into a larger container.
3. Put the citric acid, water, and white sugar into the container. Stir well.
4. To make the finished soda, combine 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.
ingredient_lines: 1 tsp (5 mL) 150+ proof unflavored spirit OR a mixture of ½ tsp (2.5 mL) gum arabic with ½ tsp (2.5 mL) water
notes: Use a clean eye dropper to measure drops. Do not use a pipette, an eye dropper previously used for dispensing medication, or a spoon to measure drops.

Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original Sparkling Water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.

You can make a Shirley Temple by mixing five crushed frozen cherries with the zest and sugar or by adding a volume of grenadine syrup for every volume of lemon-lime syrup when making the finished soda.

title: Orange Soda III
instructions:
1. Combine the spirit or gum arabic water and oils together in a small cup, mixing well. Set aside.
2. Transfer this mixture into a larger container.
3. Put the carrot powder or coloring, citric acid, water, and white sugar into the container. Stir well.
4. To make the finished soda, combine 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.
ingredient_lines: 1 tsp (5 mL) 150+ proof unflavored spirit OR a mixture of ½ tsp (2.5 mL) gum arabic with ½ tsp (2.5 mL) water
½ cup (120 mL) carrot powder OR a mixture of 24 drops of red food coloring and 24 drops of yellow food coloring
notes: Use a clean eye dropper to measure drops. Do not use a pipette, an eye dropper previously used for dispensing medication, or a spoon to measure drops.

Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original Sparkling Water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.

You can make a Shirley Temple by mixing five crushed frozen cherries with the zest and sugar or by adding a volume of grenadine syrup for every volume of lemon-lime syrup when making the finished soda.

title: Tea Extract
instructions:
1. Boil the water.
2. Steep the tea bag or loose leaf tea in the water for five minutes.
3. Remove the tea bag or strain out the tea leaves.
4. Boil the tea until 90% has evaporated and only 10% of the original volume remains.
ingredient_lines: 1 tea bag or 1 tsp (5 mL) loose leaf tea

title: Quick Sourdough Starter
instructions:
1. Mix all ingredients in a bowl until smooth.
2. Cover the bowl and place in a warm place (~70–80 °F / 20–27 °C). It should begin making some small bubbles within an hour or two (the timing depends mainly on how cold the milk is).
3. Proceed as directed for "Day 1" of your sourdough recipe.
ingredient_lines: 1 small package (0.25 ounces / 7 grams) instant dry yeast

title: Baked Mac N Cheese
instructions:
1. Cook pasta to desired texture, or to the instructions on the box.
2. Drain water from pot, after the pasta is done cooking.
3. Add liquid cheese sauce to pasta. Mix well.
4. Add pasta to pan. Sprinkle breadcrumbs, and shredded cheese on top of pasta.
5. Put pan in oven. Bake at 300 for 30 minutes or until your desired temperature.
6. Enjoy!
ingredient_lines: 3-4 boxes of shell pasta, with liquid cheese

title: Hypotonic Sports Drink
instructions:
1. Transfer the water to a clean container, such as a measuring jug.
2. Stir in the salt until fully dissolved, then mix in the cordial. Stir thoroughly until evenly mixed.
3. Chill the mixture in the fridge until cool.
4. Pour into a clean sports bottle or thermos flask and sip gradually during exercise.
notes: Make sure the cordial (squash concentrate) has enough sugar. Ideally, it should provide around 10–11 g of carbohydrates per 25 ml. This ensures the final drink is at the correct hypotonic concentration for effective hydration during exercise.

Only make what you intend to use within the same day. Sweetened cordial solutions are more stable than fresh fruit drinks, but for safety and taste, store in an airtight sealed container (preferably glass) in the fridge and consume within 48 hours.

It is fine to store this in a conventional sports bottle if you intend to drink it all within 2 hours. For longer periods, a sports thermos flask bottle is recommended; it can keep the drink cool for up to 12 hours. Ideally pre-chill your thermos flask with ice and cold water before filling.
Residues can attract bacteria over time. After drinking, ensure to wash your bottle or flask with warm soapy water and a bottle brush to prevent bacterial overgrowth.
The drink can also be frozen in ice cube trays for up to 2–3 months and thawed or made into a slushy when needed.

title: Bò bía
instructions:
1. Roast the small dried shrimps without any oil in a pan by stirring constantly on medium heat for 2 to 3 minutes until fragrant.
2. Clean the pan, fill about half full with water and bring to a boil. Cook 2 Chinese sausages for about 10 minutes to soften and remove some of the fat. Rinse the sausages well, let them cool and slide them thinly on a diagonal.
3. Crack 2 eggs in a small bowl and beat them until fluffy. Season lightly with a pinch of salt and a pinch of sugar.
4. In a non-stick pan, add 1 tsp of vegetable oil. When it's hot enough, pour in half of the egg mixture and quickly tilt the pan in a circular motion to spread the egg thinly and evenly. When one side is golden, flip it over and fry the other side for 5 more seconds. Repeat until the egg mixture has been used up.
5. Let the omelettes cool completely. Roll them up and cut into half-inch strips.
6. In a saucepan, heat up some cooking oil and sauté 1 tbsp of garlic until fragrant.
7. Add in the jicama strips and stir-fry with some salt for about 10 to 15 minutes until it turns quite translucent and tastes naturally sweet.
8. Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a small sauce pan on medium-high heat, then fry 1 tbsp minced garlic till golden brown.
9. Then add hoisin sauce, pork broth, peanut butter and sugar. Stir well and simmer on low heat for 1-2 minutes until thickened.
10. Transfer to condiment bowls and top up with minced fresh chili, pickled carrots and daikon and crushed peanuts.
11. Set up a rolling station with the prepared Chinese sausages, stir-fried jicama, omelette strips, fresh greens (e.g. lettuce and Thai basil), roasted small dried shrimps, some crushed peanuts and fried shallots ready on the plates.
12. Prepare a small bowl with pickled carrots and daikon.
13. Also prepare a large bowl of lukewarm water to soften rice paper, and a flat work surface (like a cutting board or a large plate) for the rolling job.
14. To soften the rice paper, quickly dip it into a bowl of warm water (the dipping motion should take no more than 2 seconds). Gently shake off excess water and lay it on the flat surface.
15. Place a piece of lettuce and a few basil leaves at one end of the paper, then continue to add some of the stir-fried jicama, few slices of the Chinese sausages, few omelette strips, some roasted small dried shrimps, some fried shallots and crushed peanuts.
16. Starting from the end with vegetables, roll 1-2 rounds first until you reach the center of the rice paper, then fold both sides inwards. Then continue rolling until reaching the other end of the paper.
17. Roll gently and tight enough, so that the ingredients do not fall out after one's first bite. A nice roll should show up all the colors of the ingredients inside.
18. To serve, dip the salad roll in the dipping sauce or spoon some of the sauce onto the roll and have a bite.
ingredient_lines: 400 g jicama, peeled and cut into matchsticks
category_tags: Recipes using pork broth and stock

title: Stovetop Barley II
instructions:
1. If desired, rinse barley under running water until water runs clear.
2. Place the barley in a pot, and add enough water to cover the barley by several inches. Add salt and oil.
3. Cover, and bring to a boil, skimming any foam that forms.
4. Boil until barley grains have swelled to 3 times their original size and are a semiopaque white.
5. Drain into a colander.
ingredient_lines: Neutral cooking oil (optional, to reduce foaming)

title: Oral Rehydration Solution
instructions: 1. Dissolve the salt and sugar completely in the water, stirring until fully mixed. If needed, warming the solution can help dissolve the salt and sugar.
ingredient_lines: ½ level teaspoon (~3.5 g) table salt
notes: Do not add extra salt or sugar, as this can worsen dehydration.

title: Soft Spice Cookie
instructions:
1. In a large bowl, beat eggs lightly to break the yolks as one would for scrambled eggs, then mix in the shortening. If using butter, soften it slightly beforehand by heating it a little. The shortening/egg mixture should be loose.
2. Mix in the sugar, then add the salt to the liquid mixture.
3. Mix in vanilla extract, lemon extract, coffee, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cocoa powder.
4. Add the baking powder, then slowly add the flour as needed to reach a proper doughy state (in essence, able to be shaped without sticking to one's hands too much). You may not need all of the flour, or you may even need a little more based on your eggs and how closely you measured.
5. Make balls and place onto a greased or parchment-lined pan.
6. Top each cookie with a generous amount of cinnamon-sugar.
7. Bake in a 175°C (350°F) over for between 15-20 minutes.
notes: When heating up the butter, make sure that it's only barely solid when it's mixed into the eggs.
This recipe calls for already-made liquid coffee, not powder.

title: Cola IV
instructions:
1. Mix the oils in flavor solution A in a container.
2. Transfer 1 ml of flavor solution A into another container and dilute it with the spirit or gum arabic water.
3. Mix flavor solution B in a third container.
4. Combine ½ teaspoon (2.5 ml) of the finished flavor solution A, all of flavor solution B, the white sugar, and the water to make the syrup.
5. To make the finished soda, combine 1 volume of syrup with 3 volumes of carbonated water.
ingredient_lines: 12 drops tea tree oil (optional, read important warning below)
50 ml 150+ proof unflavored spirit or a mixture of 25 ml water with 25 ml gum arabic
notes: Tea tree oil is very dangerous in large quantities. Do not, under any circumstances, increase the proportion of tea tree oil in your beverage. You may choose to omit it as it is a minor ingredient.
Use a clean eye dropper to measure drops. Do not use a pipette, an eye dropper previously used for dispensing medication, or a spoon to measure drops.

Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original Sparkling Water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.
You can substitute the caramel color with browning the sugar in a saucepan and immediately adding the other syrup ingredients immediately afterward.
You can omit the caramel color and use brown sugar or piloncillo instead.
You can substitute the wine tannins and caffeine with 2 drops of tea extract or a mixture of 2 parts water to 1 part matcha.
You can substitute the phosphoric acid with ¼ tsp (0.13 ml) citric acid.
You can make cherry cola by adding 1 tsp (5 ml) of cherry extract in step 4.
You can make vanilla cola by adding an additional teaspoon (5 ml) of vanilla extract in step 4.

attribution: Wikibooks — Cookbook:Stir-fried tomato and scrambled eggs
title: Stir-fried tomato and scrambled eggs
instructions:
1. Make a cross-shaped cut on the top of the tomatoes and blanch in boiling water.
2. After a short period of time, put the tomatoes in ice water to shock them and remove the skins.
3. Cut the tomatoes into chunks and set aside.
4. Whisk together the eggs, season to taste with a pinch of salt, and scramble them in a skillet with a little oil. Set aside after cooking process is finished.
5. Heat a little oil oil in a separate skillet, add the scallions, and sauté briefly.
6. Add the tomatoes to the scallions, and stir-fry until the tomatoes release their juices.
7. Add the scrambled eggs to the pan with the scallions and tomatoes, and let everything simmer to reduce the tomato juice.

attribution: Wikibooks — Cookbook:Turmeric Chicken and Asparagus Stir-Fry
title: Turmeric Chicken and Asparagus Stir-Fry
instructions:
1. Combine the water, honey, pepper, and salt to make the sauce. Set aside.
2. Combine the flour, turmeric, and salt together. Sprinkle over the chicken, and immediately toss to coat the chicken well.
3. Heat the oil in your pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, and cook, tossing as needed, until golden brown all over. If it starts darkening too quickly, lower the heat.
4. Add the asparagus to the pan, and season with a pinch of salt. Cook for 1–2 minutes, or until tender but still crisp. Note that the asparagus will continue cooking.
5. Stir in the prepared sauce, and simmer everything until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened to your taste (about 2–3 minutes).
6. Remove from the heat, and stir in the rice vinegar and lime juice. Adjust the seasoning with additional salt, pepper, vinegar, and lime to taste.
ingredient_lines: 1 lb boneless skinless chicken thigh, cut in 1 inch (2–3 cm) pieces
1 lb asparagus, trimmed and thinly sliced on the bias
notes: If you use a regular stainless steel skillet, have uneven heat distribution, or add the chicken on too-low heat, the meat may stick to the pan.

If you want to make this recipe gluten-free, you can replace the wheat flour with cornstarch. This will slightly change the texture of the meat and the sauce, making it somewhat more like the technique of velveting.
Adding all the dry ingredients to the chicken at once without tossing immediately can cause them to clump.

title: User:Royalesignature/Obe Ata (Yoruba Pepper Stew)
instructions:
1. Blend tomatoes, peppers, and onions roughly.
2. Heat palm oil and vegetable oil, then pour in the blended mix.
3. Fry for 15–20 minutes until reduced.
4. Add iru, seasoning, and protein.
5. Simmer until oil rises to the top.
6. Serve with rice, yam, or bread.

title: User:Royalesignature/Efo Riro (Yoruba Vegetable Soup)
instructions:
1. Blend pepper mix and set aside.
2. Heat palm oil, add iru and onions.
3. Add blended pepper and fry well.
4. Add meats and stock fish.
5. Stir in vegetables and cook briefly.
6. Serve with pounded yam or eba.

title: User:Royalesignature/Gbegiri (Yoruba Bean Soup)
instructions:
1. Boil beans until soft.
2. Blend into a smooth paste.
3. Cook with pepper and palm oil.
4. Add seasoning and simmer.
5. Serve with amala and ewedu.

title: User:Royalesignature/Ikokore (Ijebu Water Yam Porridge)
instructions:
1. Grate water yam into paste.
2. Prepare pepper sauce with palm oil.
3. Add fish and seasoning.

title: User:Royalesignature/Ojojo (Yam Fritters)
instructions:
1. Grate yam and mix with pepper and onions.
2. Heat oil.
3. Scoop mixture into oil.
4. Fry until golden brown.
5. Serve hot.

title: User:Royalesignature/Ebiripo (Cocoyam Pudding)
instructions:
1. Grate cocoyam.
2. Mix with oil and spices.
3. Wrap in leaves.
4. Steam until cooked.
5. Serve with sauce.

attribution: Wikibooks — User:Royalesignature/Obe Eja Tutu (Nigerian Fresh Fish Stew)
title: User:Royalesignature/Obe Eja Tutu (Nigerian Fresh Fish Stew)
instructions:
1. Prepare pepper mix.
2. Heat oil and cook mixture.
3. Add fish gently.
4. Simmer without breaking fish.
5. Serve with yam or rice.

title: User:Royalesignature/Adalu (Beans and Corn Porridge)
instructions:
1. Boil 3 cups of beans and 3 cup of corn together for 40 minutes.
2. Add red pepper mix it together then add Plam oil.
3. Season and simmer.
4. Serve hot.

title: User:Royalesignature/Obe Egusi (Yoruba Style)
instructions:
1. Cook pepper mix in oil.
2. Add egusi paste.
3. Add protein and seasoning.
4. Add vegetables last.
5. Serve with swallow.

title: User:Bamjos/Eba with Okra soup
instructions:
1. Slice the okra and set it aside in a bowl,
2. Wash the fish/meat and season with a half teaspoon of salt, two seasoning cubes, a cup of water, and half a cup of sliced onions. Allow it to boil together for 10-15 minutes. Remove them while leaving the stock in the pot
3. Add the Fish to the boiling pot, one more cup of water, and cook for about 10 minutes till they are soft for consumption. Add two cups of water.
4. Add 200ml of palm oil, add the crayfish, pepper, and salt to taste.
5. Add the sliced okra and stir. Drop the cooked mackerel fish on top. Allow simmering for 3-4 minutes, and you are done with this delicious soup.
6. Boil the water
7. Sprinkle the garri gradually in a circular motion to avoid clumping and star it
8. As you pour, stir immediately and continuously with a wooden spatula (omorogun) or a sturdy spoon to break up any potential lumps.

title: User:NiferO/Efo riro (Yoruba Vegetable Soup)
instructions:
1. Wash and season the meat with salt, onions, and seasoning cubes. Cook until tender and set aside.
2. Add stockfish and smoked fish to the cooked meat and simmer for about 10–15 minutes.
3. In another pot, heat the palm oil. Add sliced onions and fry lightly.
4. Add blended or sliced pepper and fry for about 10 minutes, stirring to prevent burning.
5. Add the cooked meat, fish, and some stock. Stir well and allow to simmer for 5 minutes.
6. Add crayfish and locust beans (iru), then cook for another 3–5 minutes.
7. Add the vegetables (spinach or ugu) and stir thoroughly.
8. Taste and adjust seasoning. Simmer for 3–5 minutes, then remove from heat.

title: User:Fatimah Bello/Nigerian Egusi soup
instructions:
1. Season and cook the meats: Place 700 grams assorted meat (beef, shaki, ponmo) in a pot. Add half of 2 onions (roughly chopped), 1 of 2 seasoning cubes, and a pinch of 1 teaspoons salt. Add just enough water to cover. Cook on medium heat until tender shaki takes longest, so add it first, then beef, then ponmo. Reserve the meat stock; do not discard it.
2. Prepare the pepper blend: Blend 4 scotch bonnet peppers (rodo) and 2 tatashe (red bell pepper) together with the remaining half of one 2 onions (onion) using a blender or food processor. Do not add water, blend to a coarse, thick paste. Set aside.
3. Mix the egusi paste: Place 400 grams ground egusi (melon seeds) in a bowl. Add a small amount of water just enough to bind  and mix into a thick, moldable paste. Alternatively, for the frying method, keep the egusi dry. The paste method gives a smoother texture; the frying method gives a more crumbly, textured result.
4. Fry the palm oil base: Heat 0.3 cups palm oil in a wide, heavy-bottomed pot over medium heat until it melts and shimmers about 4 minutes. Add the remaining diced 2 onions and fry until translucent and fragrant, about 3–4 minutes. Add 2 tablespoons iru (locust bean) and stir well into the oil.
5. Fry the egusi: Add the egusi paste (or dry egusi) directly into the hot palm oil. Stir to coat well. Fry on medium-low heat, stirring constantly to prevent burning. The egusi will gradually turn golden and begin to clump. Fry until it is fragrant and lightly toasted this step is crucial for depth of flavour.
6. Add pepper blend and stock: Pour the blended pepper mixture into the pot and stir well into the fried egusi. Add 1.5 cups beef or chicken stock (or reserved meat stock) to loosen the mixture. Stir thoroughly, cover, and allow to cook on medium heat. The egusi will absorb the liquid and expand.
7. Add protein: Add the cooked 700 grams assorted meat (beef, shaki, ponmo), 200 grams stockfish (panla), soaked and cleaned, and 150 grams smoked fish (eja igbe), deboned into the pot. Stir gently to incorporate all proteins evenly. Add 3 tablespoons ground crayfish and the remaining 2 seasoning cubes. Taste and adjust salt. If the soup is too thick, add a little more stock or water. Cover and simmer on low heat.
8. Add the greens and finish: Add the washed and shredded 300 grams efo tete or efo shoko (African spinach), washed and shredded to the pot. Stir in gently do not over-mix or the leaves will lose their colour. Cover for just 3–5 minutes. Do not overcook the greens. Taste one final time for salt and seasoning. The soup should be thick, rich, and deeply savoury.
9. Rest and serve: Turn off the heat and allow the soup to rest for 5 minutes before serving. This allows the flavours to settle and the egusi to finish absorbing. Serve hot with pounded yam (iyán), amala, ẹbà, or fufu.
ingredient_lines: 300 grams efo tete or efo shoko (African spinach), washed and shredded
image_files: Egusi soup with ponmo and beef.jpg

title: User:Fatimah Bello/Banga Soup (Ofe Akwu)
instructions:
1. Boil palm fruits until soft, pound to loosen flesh, squeeze out extract through a sieve and set aside
2. Season and cook assorted meat with onion and seasoning. Reserve the stock.
3. Pour palm fruit extract into a pot and cook on medium heat until it thickens and oil rises to the surface
4. Add banga spices, beletete, ataiko, and iru. Stir well.
5. Add cooked meats, stockfish, and smoked fish. Pour in reserved meat stock.
6. Add ground crayfish, blended pepper, and remaining seasoning. Simmer on low heat until thick.
7. Stir in shredded uziza leaves and cook for 3–5 minutes only.
8. Serve hot with starch, pounded yam, eba, or fufu.

attribution: Wikibooks — Cookbook:Nigerian Ofe Akwu (Palm Fruit Soup)
title: Nigerian Ofe Akwu (Palm Fruit Soup)
instructions:
1. Boil the palm fruits in water for 20–25 minutes until soft, then drain. Pound the cooked fruits in a mortar to loosen the flesh from the seeds. Add warm water{{How much}} and squeeze the mixture through a sieve. Discard the fibre and seeds. If using canned concentrate, dilute as directed.
2. Season the meat with onion, 1 seasoning cube, and salt. Add stockfish midway through cooking. Cook on medium heat until tender. Reserve the meat stock.
3. Pour palm fruit extract into a pot. Cook on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until it thickens and oil rises to the surface about 15–20 minutes
4. Add ogiri okpei, ehuru, and puréed chiles. Stir well. Add reserved cooked meat and stock, smoked fish, ground crayfish, and the remaining seasoning cube. Stir and simmer on medium heat.
5. Taste and adjust with salt. The soup should be thick, rich, and deeply orange-red. If too thick, add a little warm water and stir.
6. Stir in uziza leaf. Cook for 3–5 minutes only. Serve hot with pounded yam (iyán), eba, or fufu.
ingredient_lines: 1 kilogram fresh palm fruits (or canned palm fruit concentrate)
700 grams assorted meat (e.g. beef, shaki, goat, oxtail)
1 tablespoon ogiri okpei (fermented locust bean paste)
150 grams uziza leaf or bitter leaf, shredded

title: Nshima
instructions:
1. Boil 1 Litre of water in advance, in a Kettle or Sauce pan.
2. Once the water boils, combine 1 cup of Cornmeal or Meal as we call it, with 1 1/2 cups of cold water in a sauce pan, to make a smooth paste. A flat cooking stick is ideal for this.
3. Transfer the Cornmeal paste to the stove (set at medium high heat), and then slowly pour about 700ml of boiling water into the saucepan, stirring continuously, making sure the mixture is smooth and well combined.
4. This should lead to a smooth porridge, almost creamy. Allow this to boil for at least 10 minutes, covered.
5. Remove the cover after 10 minutes and begin to add the remaining Cornmeal to the porridge, a little at a time, making sure it is well combined, before adding some more.
6. The porridge should stiffen up quickly with each addition of Cornmeal, and you will need to exert a bit of muscle to mix this well, smoothing out any lumps that form in the process
7. Remove from the stove after the 10 minutes, and using a smooth serving spoon, scoop out the Nshima, one lump at a time and transfer into your serving dish.
ingredient_lines: 3 cups of Mealie Meal/ White Cornmeal

title: Nigerian Ewa Agoyin
instructions:
1. Cook the beans in plenty of water until they become extremely soft and mushy.
2. Stir or lightly mash the cooked beans until you get a smooth, thick, porridge-like texture. Season with salt to taste, and set aside.
3. Blend or grind dried pepper and fry it with chopped onions in a pot or pan.{{Recipe summary
4. Add salt and seasoning cubes if desired, and continue frying until the oil rises and the sauce is well cooked.
5. Spoon the hot pepper sauce over the mashed beans and serve.
ingredient_lines: 4 cups brown beans or honey beans
image_files: Beans and fried plantains with Beef02.jpg

title: User:NiferO/Chikwangue congolese cassava recipes
instructions:
1. Chop of the ends of the cassava tubers, peel them, cut them into chunks, and place them in a bowl of water to soak for three days.
2. After three days have passed, wash them several times under running water to eliminate as much bitterness as possible.
3. Add the chunks to a mortar and pestle and mash until you have a smooth paste.
4. Divide the resulting paste into fist-sized batches and on a separate banana leaf or a sheet of aluminum foil, shape each batch into oblongs that are 2 inches wide and 12 inches long, then fold, so they are wrapped.
5. Arrange the chikwanga on a steamer placed over a pot of boiling water. Cover and steam for 4 to 8 hours.
6. Serve at room temperature as a side to any Central African stew, soup, or sauce.
ingredient_lines: 2 kg of fresh or frozen cassava
Banana leaves (or aluminum foil as an alternative)
image_files: Cassava Bread - cassava cooked in leaf wrap (Kwanga, Chikwangue).jpg

title: Nigerian Miyan Giyada
instructions:
1. Season with onions, salt, and seasoning cubes, then boil until tender. Keep the stock.
2. Blend groundnuts (or use ready paste) until smooth.
3. Add the paste into the pot and allow it to cook, stirring to prevent burning.
4. Add pepper and a little palm oil or vegetable oil, then mix well.
5. Add your leafy vegetables and stir.
6. Allow the soup to cook until it thickens and oil begins to rise to the top. The soup should be thick, creamy, and rich with a nutty flavor.
7. Taste and add salt or seasoning if needed.
8. Serve with swallows like tuwo shinkafa or Tuwo dawa.
ingredient_lines: 2–3 tablespoons palm oil or vegetable oil
2 cups leafy vegetables (e.g. spinach or ugu leaf)

title: User:NoraVisser/Classic Banana Bread
instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease a 9×5-inch (23×13 cm) loaf pan with butter or non-stick spray.
2. In a large mixing bowl, mash the peeled bananas thoroughly with a fork until smooth with only small lumps remaining.
3. Stir the melted butter into the mashed banana until fully combined.
4. Mix in the sugar, beaten egg, and vanilla extract.
5. Sprinkle the baking soda and salt over the mixture and stir to combine.
6. Add the flour all at once and fold gently with a spatula until just combined. Do not overmix — a few streaks of flour are fine.
7. Fold in any optional add-ins (chocolate chips, nuts, or cinnamon) if using.
8. Pour the batter into the prepared loaf pan and smooth the top.
9. Bake for 55–65 minutes, until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean or with a few moist crumbs.
10. Remove from oven and cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack to cool completely before slicing.
ingredient_lines: ⅓ cup (75 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
½ cup (60 g) chopped walnuts or pecans
notes: Banana ripeness: Use bananas with fully brown, spotted skins for maximum sweetness. If your bananas are not ripe enough, place unpeeled bananas on a baking sheet at 300°F (150°C) for 15–20 minutes until the skins turn black.
Moisture: Do not overbake. The bread is done when the center is set; slight underbaking keeps it moist.
Storage: Wrap cooled banana bread tightly in plastic wrap and store at room temperature for up to 3 days, or refrigerate for up to 1 week.
Freezing: Slice and freeze individual portions between parchment paper for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature or toast from frozen.
Butter substitute: Substitute melted coconut oil or neutral vegetable oil for a dairy-free version.
Brown sugar variation: Replace granulated sugar with packed brown sugar for a deeper, molasses-like flavor.

title: User:NoraVisser/Lemon Blueberry Scones
instructions:
1. Preheat oven to 400°F (205°C). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
2. In a large bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and lemon zest.
3. Add the cold butter cubes to the flour mixture. Using a pastry cutter or your fingertips, cut the butter into the flour until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some pea-sized pieces remaining.
4. In a small bowl, whisk together the heavy cream, egg, and vanilla extract.
5. Pour the cream mixture over the flour mixture and stir gently with a fork until just combined. Do not overmix.
6. Fold in the blueberries gently — if using frozen berries, work quickly to prevent streaking.
7. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface. Pat it into a circle about 1 inch (2.5 cm) thick.
8. Cut the circle into 8 wedges using a sharp knife or bench scraper.
9. Place the wedges on the prepared baking sheet, spaced about 2 inches apart. Brush the tops lightly with heavy cream.
10. Bake for 18–22 minutes, until golden brown on top and bottom.
11. Cool on the pan for 5 minutes, then transfer to a wire rack.
12. Prepare the glaze by whisking together powdered sugar and lemon juice until smooth. Drizzle over slightly warm scones.
ingredient_lines: ½ cup (115 g) cold unsalted butter, cut into small cubes
½ cup (120 ml) heavy cream, plus more for brushing
1 cup (150 g) fresh or frozen blueberries (do not thaw if frozen)
notes: Cold butter is essential: Warm butter melts into the dough and produces bread-like texture rather than flaky scones. Freeze the butter for 15 minutes before cutting.
Do not overmix: Once liquid is added, mix only until the dough just comes together.
Frozen blueberries: Work fast — frozen berries can bleed purple color into the dough if handled too much.
Make ahead: Shaped unbaked scones can be refrigerated overnight and baked fresh the next morning.
Raspberry variation: Substitute blueberries with fresh raspberries for a different flavor profile.

title: User:NoraVisser/Creamy Tomato Basil Soup
instructions:
1. Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring occasionally, for 6–8 minutes until softened and translucent.
2. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
3. Add the canned tomatoes (with juices), broth, sugar (if using), oregano, and red pepper flakes. Stir to combine.
4. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
5. Remove from heat. Add the fresh basil leaves.
6. Using an immersion blender, blend the soup directly in the pot until completely smooth. Alternatively, carefully transfer in batches to a countertop blender and blend until smooth, then return to the pot.
7. Stir in the heavy cream and heat over low heat for 2–3 minutes. Do not boil after adding cream.
8. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
9. Ladle into bowls and garnish with fresh basil leaves and a drizzle of cream if desired.
ingredient_lines: 2 cans (28 oz / 800 g each) whole peeled tomatoes, preferably San Marzano
1½ cups (360 ml) vegetable broth or chicken broth
Salt and black pepper, to taste
¼ cup (10 g) fresh basil leaves, loosely packed, plus more for garnish
notes: Roasted tomato version: Roast canned or fresh tomatoes at 400°F (205°C) for 30 minutes before adding to the pot for a deeper, caramelized flavor.
Dairy-free: Substitute heavy cream with full-fat coconut milk or cashew cream.
Vegan: Use vegetable broth and a dairy-free cream substitute.
Storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days. Freeze (without cream) for up to 3 months; add cream when reheating.
Thickness: For a thicker soup, simmer longer to reduce, or add a small potato (peeled and diced) during cooking and blend it in.
Fresh tomatoes: In summer, substitute 3 lbs (1.4 kg) ripe fresh tomatoes, cored and halved. Roasting them first is recommended.

title: Cola V
instructions:
1. Boil all of the ingredients except for the vanilla extract and bitters in a pot until it becomes sticky.
2. Strain out the solids.
3. Add the vanilla extract and bitters.
4. To make the finished soda, combine 1 volume of syrup with 5 volumes of carbonated water.
ingredient_lines: ½ in. wide strip of lemon peel cut around the fruit's circumference
½ in. wide strip of lemon peel cut around the fruit's circumference
½ in. wide strip of orange peel cut around the fruit's circumference
notes: Use water from a carbonating machine or a brand of pure carbonated water such as Polar Original Sparkling Water, Great Value Seltzer Water, or Signature Select Seltzer Water. Do not use a brand of mineral water such as Perrier, San Pellegrino, or Mineragua because the added minerals will ruin the taste. Avoid flavored sparkling water such as La Croix or Spindrift because the preexisting fruit flavors will ruin the drink.
You can make cherry cola by adding five frozen cherries during step 1 or 1 tsp (5 ml) of cherry extract during step 3.
You can make vanilla cola by adding 1 tsp (5 ml) of vanilla extract during step 3.

title: Githeri
instructions:
1. Wash the maize and beans thoroughly. If using dried maize and beans, soak them overnight in separate bowls of water.
2. Drain the soaked maize and beans and place them in a large pot.
3. Add enough water to cover the mixture and boil until both the maize and beans become soft. This may take 1–2 hours depending on the type used.
4. In another pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat.
5. Add the chopped onions and cook until soft and lightly golden.
6. Stir in the garlic, tomatoes, carrot, and bell pepper. Cook for several minutes until the tomatoes soften.
7. Add curry powder or turmeric if desired.
8. Add the cooked maize and beans to the vegetable mixture and stir well.
9. Season with salt and simmer for 10–15 minutes, adding a little water if necessary.
10. Serve hot.
ingredient_lines: 2 cups dried maize kernels or fresh maize
2 cups dried beans (kidney beans, red beans, or mixed beans)
notes: Soaking dried maize and beans overnight reduces cooking time.
A pressure cooker can greatly speed up preparation.
Fresh maize gives a softer and sweeter flavour.
Fried onions improve the flavour significantly.
Leftover githeri can be reheated or fried the next day.

title: Mutura
instructions:
1. Thoroughly clean the intestines using water and salt. Rinse several times until clean.
2. Boil the chopped meat and tripe for several minutes until partly cooked.
3. Heat a pan and sauté the onions, garlic, ginger, and chilies until fragrant.
4. Combine the meat mixture with the sautéed ingredients in a bowl.
5. Add black pepper, coriander leaves, and salt.
6. Stir in the blood if using.
7. Carefully stuff the cleaned intestines with the meat mixture, avoiding overfilling.
8. Tie the ends securely with kitchen twine or thin strips of casing.
9. Grill the mutura over medium charcoal heat, turning regularly until browned and fully cooked.
10. Slice into bite-sized pieces and serve hot.
ingredient_lines: 500 g beef, goat meat, or mixed meat, finely chopped
200 g tripe or organ meat, finely chopped
notes: Properly cleaning the intestines improves flavour and hygiene.
Do not overstuff the casing, as it may burst during grilling.
Charcoal grilling gives mutura its traditional smoky flavour.
Turning the sausage regularly helps it cook evenly.
Fresh coriander and ginger improve aroma and taste.

title: Shahan ful
instructions:
1. Wash and soak the dried fava beans overnight.
2. Drain the beans and place them in a large pot with fresh water.
3. Simmer over low heat until the beans become soft and tender. Add more water if necessary.
4. Mash the cooked beans into a coarse paste using a spoon or potato masher.
5. In another pan, heat the olive oil or niter kibbeh over medium heat.
6. Add the onions and cook until soft.
7. Stir in the garlic, tomatoes, chilies, cumin, and berbere spice.
8. Cook for several minutes until fragrant.
9. Add the mashed beans and stir well.
10. Season with lemon juice, salt, and black pepper.
11. Simmer for a few minutes until thick.
12. Serve hot with yogurt, feta cheese, or fresh herbs if desired.
ingredient_lines: 2 cups dried fava beans (or canned fava beans)
2 tablespoons olive oil or niter kibbeh
Yogurt or feta cheese for serving (optional)
Bread rolls or flatbread for serving
notes: Soaking the beans overnight reduces cooking time.
Slow cooking improves flavour and texture.
Olive oil adds richness and aroma.
Canned fava beans can be used for faster preparation.
Extra chili peppers may be added for a spicier dish.

title: Ekpang Nkukwo
instructions:
1. Peel and wash the cocoyam thoroughly.{{Cite web |last=for #OunjeAladun |first=Omolabake |date=2018-04-12 |title=Ekpang Nkukwo |url=https://ounjealadun.com/2018/04/12/ekpang-nkukwo/ |access-date=2026-06-06 |website=Ounje Aladun |language=en-GB}}{{Cite web |last=ago |first=elianymemberMember {{!}} Friendin Steem4Nigeria • 3 years |date=2023-04-07 |title=How To prepare Ekpang Nkukwo - Africa delicacy |url=https://steemit.com/steem4nigeria/@eliany/how-to-prepare-ekpang-nkukwo-africa-delicacy |access-date=2026-06-06 |website=Steemit |language=en}}
2. Grate the cocoyam into a smooth paste.
3. Wash the cocoyam leaves and cut off any hard stalks.
4. Place a small quantity of the cocoyam paste in each leaf and wrap it securely.
5. pour plam oil into the cooking pot
6. Arrange the wrapped cocoyam parcels in the cooking pot that already contains plam oil.
7. Add the fish, stockfish, dry fish into the pot
8. pour in your pepper, onions, crayfish, seasoning cubes.
9. In a separate pot boil hot water that will be enough for the food.
10. put your cooking pot on fire and pour in the already boiled water into the cooking pot that contains your cocoyam parcels and ingredients and stir gently using a wooden spatula.
11. Cover the pot and let it cook on medium heat for 2-3 minutes, then you pour in your periwinkles and stri gently.
12. Cover and cook over medium heat for about 1-2 hours, adding water if necessary.
13. Stir carefully from time to time to prevent burning.
14. Continue cooking until the cocoyam is soft and the sauce is thick.
15. Serve hot.
ingredient_lines: Fresh fish, Washed and cut into pieces

title: Akpu
instructions:
1. Peel the cassava tubers and wash thoroughly.
2. Place the cassava in a container and cover completely with water.
3. Allow it to ferment for 3–4 days or until softened.
4. Remove any fibres and hard portions from the fermented cassava.
5. Mash the cassava and sieve to obtain a smooth paste.
6. Suspend the paste in a clean cloth or sack and allow excess water to drain.
7. Transfer the fermented cassava paste into a pot.
8. Cook over medium heat while stirring continuously until a smooth, stretchy dough forms.
9. Shape into portions and serve hot with soup.
notes: The duration of fermentation may vary depending on temperature.
Akpu is traditionally wrapped in leaves or packaged in nylon before sale.
Proper fermentation helps reduce the natural cyanide content of cassava.
Similar cassava-based swallows are consumed in various parts of West and Central Africa.

title: Kachumbari
instructions:
1. Gently toss together all the ingredients in a mixing bowl until well-distributed.
2. Allow the salad to rest for 5–10 minutes.
3. Taste the salad and adjust the seasoning as needed.
4. Serve fresh.
notes: If desired, additional ingredients such as avocado, mango, or bell pepper can be added.
The quantity of chiles can be adjusted to taste, depending on spice preference. Fresh lemon or lime juice gives a brighter flavor than bottled juice.
Select tomatoes that are fully ripe but still firm.
To reduce the sharp flavor of the onions, try soaking them for a few minutes in cold water before draining and incorporating them into the salad.
Prepare kachumbari shortly before serving to keep it fresh and crisp. Do not refrigerate for long periods, as the tomatoes may become watery.

title: Supu Ya Ndizi
instructions:
1. Peel and slice the green bananas into medium-sized pieces.
2. If using meat, cook it in a pot with water until tender and reserve the stock.
3. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
4. Add the onion and cook until soft and translucent.
5. Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
6. Add the tomatoes and cook until softened.
7. Stir in the curry powder.
8. Add the bananas, carrot, and potato.
9. Pour in the stock or water and bring to a boil.
10. Reduce the heat and simmer for 30–40 minutes, or until the bananas are very soft.
11. Add the cooked meat or fish if using.
12. Season with salt and black pepper.
13. Mash some of the bananas with a spoon to thicken the soup, if desired.
14. Simmer for an additional 5 minutes.
15. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.
ingredient_lines: 6 green cooking bananas, peeled and sliced
notes: Vegetarian Supu Ya Ndizi
Chicken banana soup
Fish banana soup
Coconut milk banana soup
Spicy banana soup with chili peppers

title: Wali Wa Nazi
instructions:
1. Wash the rice thoroughly until the water runs clear.
2. Soak the rice in water for 20 minutes, then drain.
3. In a cooking pot, combine the coconut milk, water, and salt.
4. Bring the mixture to a gentle boil over medium heat.
5. Add the drained rice and stir once.
6. Reduce the heat to low and cover the pot tightly.
7. Cook for 20–25 minutes, or until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender.
8. Remove the pot from the heat and allow it to rest for 5–10 minutes.
9. Fluff the rice gently with a fork before serving.
notes: Wali wa Nazi with cardamom
Wali wa Nazi with cinnamon
Brown coconut rice
Coconut rice with peas
Spiced Swahili coconut rice

title: Mchemsho (Tanzanian cuisine)
instructions:
1. Place the beef in a large pot and cover with water.
2. Add half of the onion, half of the ginger, and a pinch of salt.
3. Simmer until the meat becomes tender, about 1–1½ hours.
4. Reserve the cooking stock.
5. Heat the oil in a separate large pot.
6. Sauté the remaining onion until soft.
7. Add the garlic and remaining ginger and cook for 1 minute.
8. Stir in the tomatoes and cook until softened.
9. Add the cumin, coriander, and turmeric.
10. Add the potatoes, carrots, green bananas, green beans, cabbage, and bell pepper.
11. Pour in the reserved stock.
12. Add the cooked beef.
13. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 30–40 minutes.
14. Cook until all vegetables are tender.
15. Season with salt, black pepper, and lime juice.
16. Garnish with chopped coriander.
17. Serve hot.
ingredient_lines: 4 green cooking bananas, peeled and sliced
notes: Chicken mchemsho
Fish mchemsho
Vegetarian mchemsho
Mchemsho with eggplant
Mchemsho with coconut milk

title: Chipsi mayai
instructions:
1. Peel the potatoes and cut them into thin fries.
2. Heat oil in a deep frying pan or pot.
3. Fry the potatoes until golden brown and crispy.
4. Remove the fries and drain on paper towels.
5. In a bowl, beat the eggs until well combined.
6. Add salt and black pepper.
7. Stir in the onion, tomato, and chili if using.
8. Add the fried chips to the beaten eggs and mix gently.
9. Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
10. Pour the egg and chips mixture into the pan.
11. Cook for 3–5 minutes until the bottom is golden brown.
12. Carefully flip the omelette using a plate or lid.
13. Cook the other side for another 3–4 minutes.
14. Remove from the heat when fully cooked.
15. Garnish with fresh coriander.
16. Cut into wedges and serve hot.
ingredient_lines: 4 medium potatoes, peeled and cut into fries
2 tbsp vegetable oil (plus extra for frying)
notes: Vegetable Chipsi Mayai
Cheese Chipsi Mayai
Spicy Chipsi Mayai
Chicken Chipsi Mayai
Chipsi Mayai with bell peppers

title: Mtori (Tanzanian stew)
instructions:
1. Place the beef and water in a large pot.
2. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer until the meat is tender, about 1–1½ hours.
3. Remove the meat from the stock and set aside.
4. Add the bananas, onion, carrot, bell pepper, and potato to the stock.
5. Cook until the bananas become very soft.
6. Return the cooked meat to the pot.
7. Add the ginger, garlic, salt, and black pepper.
8. Simmer for 10 minutes.
9. Mash the bananas using a wooden spoon or potato masher until a thick, creamy consistency is achieved.
10. Stir in the butter or margarine.
11. Adjust seasoning to taste.
12. Simmer for another 5 minutes.
13. Garnish with fresh coriander and serve hot.
ingredient_lines: 6–8 green cooking bananas (plantains), peeled and sliced
notes: Chicken mtori
Goat meat mtori
Coconut milk mtori
Vegetarian mtori
Spicy mtori with chili peppers

title: Xarém (Porridge dish)
instructions:
1. Rinse the clams thoroughly and discard any damaged shells.
2. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
3. Cook the bacon until lightly browned.
4. Add the sausage and cook for 2–3 minutes.
5. Stir in the onion and cook until softened.
6. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
7. Pour in the white wine and add the bay leaf.
8. Add the clams, cover the pot, and cook until the shells open.
9. Remove the clams and set aside.
10. Strain the cooking liquid and return it to the pot.
11. Add the stock or water and bring to a boil.
12. Gradually add the cornmeal while stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
13. Reduce the heat and cook for 20–25 minutes, stirring frequently.
14. Return the clams, bacon, and sausage to the pot.
15. Stir in the coriander.
16. Season with salt and black pepper.
17. Serve hot.
ingredient_lines: 4 cups fish stock, chicken stock, or water
100 g chouriço or smoked sausage, sliced
notes: Xarém com Conquilhas (with clams)
Xarém with shrimp
Xarém with mussels
Xarém with pork cracklings
Vegetarian xarém
Xarém with sardines

title: Agidi (Nigerian Cornstarch Swallow)
instructions:
1. Gradually mix the water into the corn starch until you get a smooth, lump-free mixture.{{Cite web |last=Nigeria |first=Guardian |date=2024-01-28 |title=How To Make White Agidi (Eko) Recipe |url=https://guardian.ng/life/how-to-make-white-agidi-eko-recipe/ |access-date=2026-06-03 |website=The Guardian Nigeria News - Nigeria and World News |language=en-GB}} If desired, add a little sugar to taste.
2. Transfer the mixture to a pot, and stir continuously over medium-low heat until it thickens to a smooth, custard-like consistency.
3. Add a little water around the sides of the pot, cover, and simmer for about 10 minutes
4. Stir well, and test for doneness by placing a small portion in cold water; if it sets firmly after cooling, the agidi is ready.
5. Transfer the mixture into containers or wrap in leaves, then allow it to cool completely and set before serving.

title: Scorched rice
instructions:
1. Rinse the rice thoroughly until the water runs clear.
2. Soak the rice for 20–30 minutes if desired, then drain.
3. Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy-bottomed pot.
4. Add the rice and cook until most of the water has been absorbed.
5. Reduce the heat to very low.
6. Drizzle the oil or melted butter around the edges of the pot.
7. Cover the pot tightly with a lid.
8. Continue cooking for 20–30 minutes without stirring.
9. Allow a golden-brown crust to form on the bottom of the pot.
10. Remove the pot from the heat and let it rest for 5 minutes.
11. Carefully loosen the rice from the sides of the pot.
12. Invert onto a serving plate or gently remove the crispy layer with a spatula.
13. Serve immediately.
ingredient_lines: 2 tbsp vegetable oil, butter, or other cooking fat
notes: Persian Tahdig
Korean Nurungji
Spanish Socarrat
Chinese Guōbā
Dominican Concón
Panamanian Concolón
Iraqi Hikakeh

title: Bafa (Cape Verdean Seafood Stew)
instructions:
1. Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
2. Add the onion and cook until softened.
3. Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
4. Add the tomatoes and bell pepper and cook until tender.
5. Stir in the paprika, black pepper, and chili flakes.
6. Add the octopus pieces and cook for 5 minutes.
7. Pour in the white wine and allow it to simmer for 2–3 minutes.
8. Add the fish stock and bay leaf.
9. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer for 45 minutes.
10. Add the clams or mussels.
11. Cover and cook until the shellfish open, about 5–10 minutes.
12. Discard any shellfish that do not open.
13. Season with salt to taste.
14. Stir in the chopped parsley.
15. Remove the bay leaf.
16. Serve hot with lemon wedges.
ingredient_lines: 1 kg octopus, cleaned and cut into pieces
notes: Bafa de Polvo (octopus bafa)
Bafa with limpets
Bafa with whelks
Mixed seafood bafa
Spicy bafa with extra chili peppers

title: Msemmen
instructions:
1. Mix the flour, semolina, salt, sugar, and yeast in a bowl.
2. Gradually add warm water and knead until a smooth dough forms.
3. Divide the dough into small balls and let rest for 30 minutes.
4. Flatten each ball into a thin sheet.
5. Brush with oil and butter, then fold into a square.
6. Let the folded squares rest for 15 minutes.
7. Flatten gently and cook on a hot griddle until golden brown on both sides.
8. Serve warm with honey, jam, tea, or savory accompaniments.
notes: M'semen (also spelled Msemen or Msemmen) is a traditional layered flatbread from the Maghreb, especially Morocco and Algeria.
It is commonly served for breakfast or tea time.

title: Mukimo
instructions:
1. Place the potatoes, maize, and peas in a large pot and cover with water.
2. Bring to a boil and cook until the potatoes are tender.
3. Add the chopped vegetables and continue cooking for 5–10 minutes.
4. Drain excess water if necessary.
5. Mash all the ingredients together until well combined.
6. Season with salt to taste.
7. Serve hot with beef stew, chicken stew, or grilled meat.
ingredient_lines: 2 cups pumpkin leaves, spinach, or kale, chopped
notes: Mukimo is a staple dish in Kenya, particularly in the central highlands.
Different regions use different leafy greens depending on local availability.
Some versions include beans instead of peas.

title: Bobotie
instructions:
1. Soak the bread in the milk and set aside.
2. Heat the oil in a frying pan and sauté the onion until soft.
3. Add the minced meat and cook until browned.
4. Stir in the curry powder, turmeric, chutney, vinegar, raisins, salt, and pepper.
5. Squeeze excess milk from the bread and mix the bread into the meat mixture.
6. Transfer the mixture to a greased baking dish.
7. Beat the eggs with the milk and pour over the meat.
8. Place the bay leaves on top.
9. Bake at 180°C (350°F) for about 35–40 minutes, or until the custard is set and lightly browned.
10. Serve hot with yellow rice, vegetables, or chutney.
ingredient_lines: Salt and black pepper, to taste
notes: Bobotie is believed to have originated from Cape Malay cuisine in South Africa.
The combination of sweet and savory flavors is characteristic of the dish.
Traditionally, it is served with yellow rice flavored with turmeric.

title: Bunny Chow
instructions:
1. Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat.
2. Add the onion and cook until softened.
3. Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook for 1 minute.
4. Add the curry powder, turmeric, and paprika. Stir until fragrant.
5. Add the meat or vegetables and cook until lightly browned.
6. Add the tomatoes and cook until softened.
7. Add the potatoes and water, and season with a little salt and pepper.
8. Simmer for 30–40 minutes, or until the meat and potatoes are tender and the sauce has thickened. Adjust the seasoning as necessary.
9. Cut the loaf of bread into halves or quarters, and remove part of the soft interior from each piece to create a cavity.
10. Fill the bread cavity generously with hot curry.
11. Garnish with coriander if desired and serve immediately.
ingredient_lines: 500 g (1 lb) beef, mutton, chicken, or mixed vegetables, cut in pieces
1 large, unsliced loaf of white bread
notes: The curry may be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 3 days. Assemble the bunny chow shortly before serving to prevent the bread from becoming soggy.

title: Asaro
instructions:
1. Blend the tomatoes, peppers, and onion into a smooth purée.
2. Heat the oil in a pot and add the purée. Cook for about 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
3. Stir in seasoning cubes, salt, and any protein being used.
4. Stir in the water and bring to a boil.
5. Gently stir in the cubed yam. Cover and simmer, stirring occasionally, until the yam becomes soft and some of it has broken down to thicken the dish.
6. Add leafy vegetables if desired and cook for an additional 3–5 minutes.
7. Adjust seasoning and remove from heat.
ingredient_lines: ½ cup palm oil or vegetable oil
200 g protein, such as fresh fish, meat, or smoked fish (optional)
1 medium (about 1 kg) yam, peeled and cubed
Leafy vegetables such as spinach or ugu (optional)
notes: Do not over-stir during cooking, as this may cause all the yam pieces to break apart. The dish should be thick and creamy but still contain visible yam chunks.
Fresh stock can be used to enhance flavor.
The amount of chile pepper can be adjusted according to personal taste.

title: Scottish Porridge
instructions:
1. Mix the steel-cut oats with a teaspoon of buckwheat flour in a bowl.
2. Add warm water to soak the oats and add a splash of lemon juice or apple cider vinegar. Cover and allow to soak overnight or at least 7 to 8 hours.
3. Place the oats, salt and water into a small pan and gently bring it to a small boil, stirring occasionally until the porridge starts to thicken.
4. Once the thickening has begun, lower the heat to low to avoid burning the porridge and allow it to simmer for approximately 15 to 20 minutes (or less if the oats are tender and reached your preferred consistency).
5. Remove from the heat and let it stand for 1 or 2 minutes before serving.
6. Serve and top with your choice of toppings, such as chia seeds, walnuts, tablespoon of peanut butter, berries, cinnamon, or a dollop of Greek yogurt.
ingredient_lines: ½ cup (80 g) steel-cut oats, also called Irish oats
1 teaspoon lemon juice or apple cider vinegar (for soaking)
1 teaspoon of buckwheat flour (for reducing phytates)
notes: Traditionalists uses whole-oat groats and mill them to make Scottish porridge. However store bought steel-cut oats are a reliable substitute for those who do not possess a mill. If you possess a mill and desire the authentic Scottish taste, you can swap steel-cut oats and use milled whole-oat groats instead.
Pre-soaking is essential to achieve a soft, velvety texture as it helps break down starches in oats and soften its hearty outer hull.

To reduce phytates in oats, you should add both an acidic medium and a phytase-rich ingredient to your soaking liquid, This can be achieved by adding a teaspoon of buckwheat flour and a teaspoon of apple cider vinegar.

Ideally you should start your soak with warm water (but not boiling as that kills enzymes) and leave it out to soak at room temperature for 16 to 24 hours. However, a shorter 8 to 12 hours can still significantly reduce anti-nutrients and make your breakfast much easier on your stomach.

After soaking, rinsing reduces starch, apple cider vinegar or lemon juice, and any available pesticide residue. If you are using organic oats and want maximum nutrition and creaminess, you can skip the rinse.

Always cover the bowl with cling wrap when soaking oats. This is to both to keep out potential contaminants (brought in by outside flies, dusts, bad bacteria, etc), as well as keeping the oats from drying out by preventing the evaporation of the top layer of water. If top oats are exposed to air and are dried out, they will be unable to benefit from buckwheat enzymes.

Salt is essential to a good Scottish porridge as it brings out the earthy flavor of the oats. There is however a difference in opinion on when it is best to add in the salt. Some argue that it's better to add a pinch halfway through cooking whilst others believe it's best added at the very beginning of the cooking process. Feel free to experiment and choose the one that you prefer though it is just a myth that oats cannot cook properly if you add salt in very early.
When serving, try to opt for shallow bowls as they help quickly cool down the porridge evenly whereas deeper bowls tend to keep the centre of the porridge dangerously hot.
Opt to start with cold water for cooking. Avoid cooking with milk as milk sugars tend to both mask the clean grain taste and it scorches easily.

title: Crotopo Soup
instructions:
1. Pound the veal in a mortar.
2. Add ham with some fat in it, the egg yolk, salt, pepper, and very little nutmeg, and pound some more.
3. Pass through a sieve.
4. Cut the rolls into slices and spread them with the meat mixture.
5. Place them in the oven and bake until colored.
6. Cut the rolls in halves or quarters, and place them in a tureen.
7. Just before serving, pour a very good clear broth over them.

title: Idiyappam (South Indian Rice Noodles)
instructions:
1. Mix rice flour with hot water and salt.
2. Knead it into a smooth dough.
3. Press the dough through an idiyappam presser or sieve onto banana leaves on which a little grated coconut has been sprinkled. Alternatively, press it directly onto an idli pan without banana leaves.
4. Steam for 5–10 minutes. Some people add a little grated coconut on top before steaming.
ingredient_lines: 1 cup raw (i.e. not roasted) rice flour
1 cup water (hot water preferred by some)
notes: Idiyappams may be served with egg curry or brown chickpea (kadala) curry. In some places it is eaten dipped in fresh coconut milk mixed with sugar.

title: Jerk Lobster
instructions:
1. Thinly slice the scallions.
2. Melt the butter in a small skillet.
3. Lightly sauté the scallions until golden.
4. Add the lemon juice.
5. Add Jamaica pickapeppa sauce or hot pepper sauce (optional, depending on your taste).
6. Let it simmer for about 1 minute, then set aside.
7. Remove the membrane from the lobster tails.
8. Use a sharp knife to split the lobster tail in half lengthwise.
9. Brush butter sauce onto each tail.
10. Using the same brush, spread the jerk sauce over the tails, especially on the exposed meat. Set oven to broil.
11. Put the lobster tails in oven on the meat side for 4 minutes, turn, and cook the shell side for 2 minutes.
12. If you want a more smoked taste, cook for 2 minutes on each side in the oven, then place on a barbecue grill for 3 minutes. You may need to add more jerk sauce if using a grill.
13. Serve with Jamaican festival and/or bammy. You can also serve with Jamaican hardo bread.
ingredient_lines: 2 tsp lemon juice or lime juice
½ tsp Jamaican pickapeppa sauce or 3 drops of Jamaican hot pepper sauce (optional)

attribution: Wikibooks — Cookbook:Mashed Plantains and Pork Rinds (Mofongo)
title: Mashed Plantains and Pork Rinds (Mofongo)
instructions:
1. Peel the plantains and cut into 1-inch diagonal pieces.
2. Heat the oil in a large skillet. Place the plantains in the oil and fry on both sides (approximately 3 ½ minutes per side).
3. Remove the plantains from the pan and flatten the plantains by placing a plate over the fried plantains and pressing down.
4. Return the plantains to the hot oil and fry 1 minute on each side. Then, place on paper towels.
5. While the plantains are still hot, use a mortar and pestle to mash them with the garlic, fat, and stock or broth. Add the chicharrones, salt, and pepper to taste.
ingredient_lines: ½ pound pork rinds, also known as chicharrones or pork cracklings, ground
1 tablespoon fat (e.g. olive oil, butter, or lard)
notes: Packaged pork rinds can be used. Alternatively, any kind of bacon can also be used.

You can also use a food processor for mashing; add the plantains to food processor with bacon, garlic and some salt and pepper. You may have to work in batches. Process to consistency of mashed—not whipped—potatoes. Do not over-process!

attribution: Wikibooks — Cookbook:Pasta, Meat and Cheese Casserole (Mostaccioli)
title: Pasta, Meat and Cheese Casserole (Mostaccioli)
instructions:
1. Cook mostaccioli until al dente in boiling salted water. Drain and set aside.
2. In skillet, combine meat, sausages, onion, green pepper and garlic. Cook while breaking up meat, until browned. Drain off fat.
3. To the meat, add all remaining ingredients, except egg and cheeses. Bring meat sauce to a boil. Reduce heat.
4. Cover and simmer for 15–20 minutes, stirring occasionally.
5. Combine egg and cheeses. To assemble, stir cooked pasta into meat sauce. Place half in buttered 1-quart baking dish.
6. Spread cheese mixture evenly over the top. cover with remaining pasta.
7. Bake, covered, at 350°F for 30–35 minutes or until cooked through.

title: Shirred Egg
instructions:
1. Butter a shirred egg dish (a small casserole or custard dish).
2. Put the dish on a low heat to melt the butter, or just add 2–3 tsp cream.
3. Break an egg in the dish over the cream and season with salt and pepper.
4. Optionally, sprinkle with shredded cheese and/or bread crumbs.
5. Bake in the oven at 375°F long enough to set the whites of the eggs. Alternatively, cook by placing the dish directly on low heat.
6. Serve in the same dish.

attribution: Wikibooks — Cookbook:Deep Fried Chickpea Dough Balls (Chyueeam)
title: Deep Fried Chickpea Dough Balls (Chyueeam)
instructions:
1. Soak kadalai paruppu in clean water for at least 8 hours. They will double in size, so allow extra water for them to soak up.
2. Boil kadalai paruppu. This should take about 40 minutes in a regular pot on the stove, or about 9 minutes in a pressure cooker (plus 10 minutes to depressurise).
3. Grind boiled kadalai paruppu with the jaggery and elachi, without adding any water, to make a dough.
4. Make small balls with the dough.
5. Make a thin batter with the maida and water. Add salt as needed.
6. Dip the dough balls in the batter.
7. Pour the oil in a pan. Heat until a small piece of dough floats and bubbles when added.
8. Add a few battered dough balls. Deep fry individually until golden.
ingredient_lines: ½ kg kadalai paruppu (Bengal gram, small brown chickpeas)
½ kg vellam (jaggery, unrefined palm sugar)
½ kg maida mavu (refined wheat flour)

title: Atkins-Friendly Mock Tiramisu
instructions:
1. Blend everything together until smooth.
2. Enjoy!

title: Atkins-Friendly Chocolate Mousse
instructions:
1. Lightly whip half and half and cream in a blender.
2. Add other ingredients into blender.
3. Blend everything together until smooth.
4. Enjoy.
ingredient_lines: 1 cup (240 ml) or 1 part half and half
1 cup (240 ml) or 1 part heavy cream
4 scoops or 1 part Atkins Chocolate Shake Mix
2 tsp or 1/24 part stevia extract or other sugar replacement

attribution: Wikibooks — Cookbook:Menudo (Mexican Tripe and Hominy Soup)
title: Menudo (Mexican Tripe and Hominy Soup)
instructions:
1. Wipe the dried Anchos off with a wet paper towel.
2. If desired, toast dried chilies on each side 15 seconds on a hot griddle (this releases essential oils and enhances the flavor).
3. Place the dried chilies into the small pot of boiling water and boil for 10 minutes, turning frequently in the boiling water to ensure all sides receive their fair share of punishment.
4. Remove the chili pot from the stove and drain off the boiling water. Fill with cold water; let it sit a few minutes to cool.
5. Remove the stems from the chilies, cut chilies longitudinally from stem to tip on one side and open. Flush gently with running cold water to remove the seeds.
6. Place stemless and seedless reconstituted chilies into a blender and purée.
7. Remove pure from the blender and place in the refrigerator overnight.
8. Rinse and drain the white hominy.
9. Place the patas (feet) and ribs into a pot.
10. Place the hominy in the pot with the patas (feet).
11. Put 1 tbsp salt in the pot.
12. Take 3–4 dried Chilis de Arbol, discard the seeds and stems, and snip the chilis into ringlets and put into the pot.
13. Cover with water to a height not exceeding 1 cm above the ingredients and bring to a boil.
14. Cook the posole uncovered until the ribs are finished. Remove from the heat.
15. Remove the meat from the ribs and dice into small cubes, place back into the pot with the posole, discard the bones.
16. Place the cooked patas (feet) into the pressure pot you will use to make the menudo.
17. Place a small pot of water on the stove and set to boil. This will be needed to prepare the chilies.
18. Cut the fat from off of the tripe. If fat clings to the non-honeycombed side of the tripe, use a stiff brush to remove it.
19. Cut tripe into small pieces, about ¾–1 inch. Strong scissors work well here!
20. If the tripe smells overly rank (this is normal), you may want to soak it in clean water for an hour (or possibly boil it in water for five minutes) throwing away the soak (boiling) water.
21. Place cut tripe into the pressure cooker on top of the patas (feet).
22. Add the garlic, bay leaves, and Mexican oregano.
23. Fill pressure cooker with water until about 1 cm. above the height of the stew ingredients.
24. Cook at pressure 35–40 minutes.
25. After the stew has cooked in the pressure cooker at full pressure for 35–40 minutes, remove from the heat and let the pot cool off completely until pressure returns to ambient.
26. Remove the patas from the pot and remove the bones. Put deboned patas into pot with the tripe and discard the bones.
27. Transfer the stew to a large bowl and add the posole, ensure all savory pieces lie below the waterline, and set in the refrigerator overnight.
28. In the morning, skim all hardened fat from the surface of the stew which has probably gelatinized overnight.
29. Reheat a serving portion of the stew in the microwave or on stovetop. When hot, place into a serving bowl.
30. Add a tablespoon of chili to the stew and blend thoroughly.
31. The menudo is ready to serve with hot corn tortillas. The spices (oregano and chili flakes) are traditionally combined before serving and placed at the side of the bowl of menudo with a lime wedge for the diner to add just prior to eating. Along with the spices, diced onion or cilantro are also traditionally added to the stew just prior to enjoying.
ingredient_lines: 2 tbsp red pepper flakes (with the seeds)
notes: Almost all (but not all) store-bought honeycomb tripe will smell strongly from the bleaching lime as possible. Let your nose be the judge as to whether or not it will require a soaking or boil as described in the steps below.
You may use cow feet instead of pig feet.

title: Yeasted Rolls II
